chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hurayz, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The prayer is not repeated except for five [issues]: purity, the time, the Qibla, the bowing, and the prostration. Then he (peace be upon him) added: Recitation is a sunnah, the Tashahhud is a sunnah, and the Takbir is a sunnah, and the sunnah does not invalidate the obligatory act.
ai.seo_question: What are the five conditions that require renewing the Islamic prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the five pillars that constitute the essential structure of prayer, distinguishing them from the sunnah acts like recitation and tashahhud which do not invalidate the prayer if omitted. This distinction reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the validity of the core obligatory acts (arkan) versus the recommended acts, ensuring that minor omissions do not nullify the worship. The narration underscores the importance of ritual purity and correct orientation as foundational elements, linking physical preparation directly to the spiritual validity of the prayer.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-36 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Hammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Hurayz, on the authority of Zurarah that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “Do not say your prayer again except for five issues: purity; proper time; the proper direction (of the Qibla) to which you turn to pray; the bowing down; and the prostration.”

Then he (MGB) added, “Reciting, the Tashahhud and the Takbir (saying God is Great) are due to the Prophet’s tradition. What is done based on the Prophet’s tradition is not contradictory to God’s ordinance.”
